summary: Iteration 3 — validated kernel-backed backend routes and the templated diplomacy pouch UI end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest passed (test_kernel_diplomacy.py) covering full game loop (create-game → 2 joins auto-fill to 3, state shape with systems/player_resources/kernel/ready_players/turn_deadline/game_over, fleet order accepted, ready→turn advance, replay snapshots) and full diplomacy ops (send→open message, counter→countered+new open, accept→kernel.pacts entry + accepted status, decline). Frontend: Create-Game→Start-Game→Activity phase reached; header-diplomacy-btn visible; overlay opens with 2 peer entries; compose form opens with Topic=trade; give-chon + give-sys + request-sys populated; Send succeeded with no error; Solo Mode toggled → header-player-selector revealed; switched to recipient; overlay reopened; TermsView correctly rendered 'You receive 2 CHON — lands at Vela Delta' and 'You give 1 CHON — lands at Mire Tau'; Accept/Decline/Counter-offer buttons all present with correct data-testids. The Accept click in the E2E script surfaced a kernel validation error ('You do not border Mire Tau, so you cannot land a delivery there.') because the compose dropdown for request-sys is filtered from the SENDER'S visible-systems (fog-of-war basic) — so systems shown to Alice as 'peer landing candidates' aren't guaranteed to actually border the peer's real territory. Backend accept path is validated (test_04_alice_accepts_counter passes) when each side picks its own state-visible landing system. This is likely a spec constraint of templated offers under FOW, not a code bug — flagged for review.

integration_issues.issue: Sender's compose request-sys dropdown lists 'peer landing candidates' computed from the sender's own visible-systems (fog-of-war basic). Under FOW the sender may not see the peer's real borders, so a selected request-sys can be a system the recipient does NOT actually border, causing kernel to correctly reject the accept with 'You do not border <sys>, so you cannot land a delivery there.' Recommend either (a) filtering the dropdown to only systems the peer is guaranteed to border (i.e., visible to sender AND known-adjacent to a peer-owned system as seen by sender), or (b) surfacing a clearer sender-side hint (e.g., '?' visibility marker on options that may not be valid for the recipient) so senders don't compose non-fulfillable offers.

issues: Landing systems the viewer cannot see are rendered as '??? ' in the terms block (e.g. '2 CHON — lands at ???'). Considered acceptable / intentional (FOW), noting for design review.

action_items: Consider filtering diplomacy-compose-request-sys options to systems that provably border a peer-owned system in the sender's visible state (or annotate uncertain ones) so the sender doesn't compose an offer the recipient cannot accept — see integration_issues.

OPTIONAL: When the recipient side receives an offer with a give/request system they cannot see, the terms row shows '??? '. Consider adding a tooltip explaining the system is out of your sensor range.
critical_code_review_comments: kernel_bridge.py: subprocess call to node CLI on every kernel op — synchronous 120s timeout. Acceptable for MVP; if latency matters, consider a persistent Node subprocess with stdin/stdout newline-delimited JSON to avoid per-op fork/exec.

kernel_api.py:_maybe_resolve: calls resolveIfDue → replayFrame → skipReport in sequence — three separate node invocations per state fetch when a turn resolves. Consider merging into one kernel op to reduce subprocess overhead on hot paths.
kernel_api.py: matches dict is in-process memory only (persistence.GameDAO is imported but never wired). Any backend restart loses all games — acknowledged in review_request but worth capturing.

kernel_api.py:diplomacy_send builds args with fromId=payload.get('player_id'); ensure Pydantic validation eventually rejects missing player_id (currently defaults to None and the kernel returns an error — works but could be more explicit).

DiplomacyPouch.jsx compose form: request-sys candidates computed from the sender's fogged view (landingCandidates(systems, peer)) can include systems that don't actually border the peer's real territory — see integration_issues action item.
App.js:3325 combat-reports button hidden when count==0 (pre-existing, iteration_2 note still applies).
PRE-EXISTING (iterations 1+2): duplicate React key warnings for connection lines still likely present in renderGalaxyMap (no fresh evidence collected this run — not in scope).
seed_data_creation: Each test creates a fresh in-memory game via /api/create-game + 2x /api/join-game (auto-fills to 3-player match).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Kernel is sealed Node CLI; do NOT modify packages/consilium-kernel. Diplomacy state fields: systems entries use 'owner' (not 'owner_id') and 'connections' (not 'neighbors'); fleets are in system.starfleet_details with 'owner'. To pick a valid landing system for player P: find a P-owned system, then a connection to a system P does NOT own with visibility='full'. In frontend, the Lobby shows a Start Game button after 3/3 players — must click that to enter activity phase (game does NOT auto-start on 3rd join in the UI, though backend marks started=true; the UI still displays the lobby until Start Game is clicked).
